transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-01-20 15:00 UTC | Duration ~36m | Attendees: Liam, Sofia (Redwood) — Maya, Tom, Priya, Ben (Starlight)

Auto-generated Summary: Weekly POC security and compliance check-in. Focused on SSO, audit logs, SOC2 deliverables, and retention windows.

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Maya: Maya here, CISO, hello.
[00:08] Tom: Tom, infra.
[00:10] Priya: Priya, data eng.
[00:12] Ben: Ben, PM.
[00:14] Liam: Great, Liam from Redwood, and Sofia's with me — we'll run through outstanding security items from the POC.
[01:02] Sofia: Quick agenda: SAML/SSO status, audit logs and retention, SOC2 artifacts, KMS questions, and any blockers.
[01:45] Maya: high level we need SSO first — procurement won't sign off without SSO + SAML metadata. also need clear audit log retention, and SOC2 evidence.
[02:10] Liam: understood. Priya, did you manage to provision the IdP test account?
[02:20] Priya: I'm working on it, we hit a small issue with the entityID mismatch from the Redwood sample — looks like the metadata URL is different than expected, I'll share details after.
[03:00] Sofia: we do have a SAML metadata endpoint; we can also provide a metadata XML if that helps. The current Redwood private deployment supports SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows.
[03:22] Ben: Quick question — if we go hosted initially, does Redwood support SAML for hosted tenants or is SAML only on Private?
[03:35] Liam: Good question. Hosted supports SAML via SSO for enterprise customers — it's routed through our control plane, but we can also do a Private deployment for stricter network controls. We'll note the security tradeoffs.
[04:10] Tom: Network wise, we prefer VPC peering or private link; public-hosted with SAML is OK if the data residency and encryption controls are validated.
[04:35] Maya: and we need audit logs to be tamper-evident and exportable to our SIEM, ideally in near real-time. retention default should be configurable.
[05:05] Sofia: We emit structured audit logs for auth events, model invocations, and admin changes. We can push to customer S3, or send to an endpoint/forwarder — we also support pushing to CloudWatch/GCP logging.
[05:40] Priya: Can you share sample logs? field names, timestamps, user identifiers — we need to map to our SIEM.
[05:52] Liam: Absolutely — action item, we'll share a sample audit-log payload plus retention config options.
[06:30] Ben: Regarding PII — do logs contain any request payloads or PII? We need to ensure tokens or sensitive prompt data aren't stored in clear.
[06:48] Sofia: By default we redact full request bodies from audit logs; we log metadata (timestamps, user_id, model, request size, truncated hashes). For customers on Dedicated/Private, you can choose full retention or redaction policies.
[07:25] Maya: We also require encryption at rest and key control — does Redwood support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
[07:40] Liam: Yes, we have KMS integrations. For hosted, we support customer-managed keys in major cloud KMS; for Private we can integrate HSM. We'll include the KMS architecture doc.
[08:10] Tom: Good. On SOC2 — can you send your latest Type II report and any gap remediation notes? procurement needs that before any contract.
[08:25] Sofia: We'll send the SOC2 Type II report and the trust pack. note: some details in the report are redacted for third parties but we can provide a cover letter and any supplemental evidence where possible.
[09:00] Priya: For the POC test itself, we want to run an audit-log ingestion test where Redwood streams logs to our S3 bucket and we verify ingestion and schema mapping. How quickly can that be set up?
[09:22] Liam: We can stand up a short test in 24–48 hours once you provide an S3 bucket or endpoint and credentials for a test IAM role.
[09:45] Priya: I'll share the S3 details today.
[10:05] Ben: Any latency impacts from audit logging, e.g., will it add overhead to inference latency?
[10:20] Sofia: No measurable token latency — logging is asynchronous. There is a tiny CPU overhead for event serialization but it's not on the critical path. In Dedicated mode you can configure batching.
[11:00] Maya: About data retention — regulatory: we need 7 years for certain records, but minimal retention for ephemeral prompts. We need the ability to set different retention windows per data class.
[11:25] Liam: We support per-data-class retention policies: logs, request payloads (if enabled), embeddings, and model outputs. For hosted customers we have default tiers and for Dedicated/Private you can configure arbitrary retention.
[12:05] Priya: Do you support automatic purging with proofs of deletion or is it manual?
[12:18] Sofia: Automatic purging is supported. For audit we can provide deletion logs and timestamps; for Dedicated we can also provide verifiable deletion events.
[12:55] Tom: KMS integration, how granular is key usage logging? we need to see which key decrypted what when investigating.
[13:10] Liam: Key usage logs are handled by the customer's KMS — Redwood emits metadata linking operations to KMS key IDs and operation IDs so you can correlate. We'll include an example mapping.
[13:40] Maya: Are there any known compliance gaps for fintech workloads?
[13:55] Sofia: No major gaps off the shelf; for higher regulated needs we recommend Private with customer KMS and VPC-only routing. We'll put together a checklist for fintech requirements.
[14:30] Ben: procurement asked about background checks and developer access controls for Redwood engineers on Dedicated — what's the policy?
[14:50] Liam: For Dedicated we enforce least-priv access and provide RBAC. We can restrict Redwood staff access and offer support via jumpbox or audited sessions. We'll include our personnel access policy summary.
[15:30] Priya: On RBAC — can we map to our existing roles via SCIM?
[15:42] Sofia: Yes, SCIM provisioning is supported for user management and role mapping.
[16:05] Tom: One more network question — for Private do you support air-gapped on-prem?
[16:20] Liam: We do offer an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments — it's heavier but doable for highly regulated customers.
[16:45] Maya: For now we'll aim for hosted with enterprise SAML + VPC peering to speed rollout, then evaluate Dedicated if needed.
[17:10] Ben: timeline check — procurement wants security docs this week; tech team wants to run the log ingestion test this week as well. is that realistic?
[17:28] Liam: Yes — SOC2 docs and compliance pack will go out tomorrow. SE will prep sample logs and ingestion plan within 48 hours.
[18:02] Sofia: I'll attach sample log schema and an example JSON payload in the follow-up email.
[18:20] Priya: note — after we ingest we'll validate schema and check SIEM mapping, may ask for minor field name changes.
[18:42] Liam: that's fine — we can adjust.
[19:00] Maya: can you confirm which artifacts you will share? list them now so procurement has it.
[19:12] Liam: Sure: SOC2 Type II report, trust pack (encryption, KMS), personnel access policy summary, SAML integration guide, sample audit logs and retention config, and a short network architecture doc for hosted vs dedicated.
[19:40] Ben: perfect. also pricing question — if we choose hosted with a dedicated SSO tenant versus Dedicated capacity, what's the delta on cost and SLA?
[20:05] Liam: We'll follow up with a concise pricing comparison. Hosted with enterprise features is usage-based; Dedicated has reserved monthly commits and higher SLA. We'll send a breakdown in the next 48 hours.
[20:38] Sofia: quick note on logs: default retention for hosted is 90 days for standard logs, but we can extend. We'll include retention tiers: 30/90/365/7 years and associated costs.
[21:05] Tom: regulatory may require 7 years for some audit trails — thanks, good to know that's supported.
[21:35] Priya: small tech nit: will the logs include per-request trace IDs to correlate across systems?
[21:48] Sofia: yes we emit trace IDs and request hashes to allow correlation.
[22:10] Maya: ok, next steps recap?
[22:18] Liam: Recap — Redwood: send SOC2 + trust pack (due tomorrow), send sample audit logs and retention options (48h), provide SAML guide and we'll wait for Priya's metadata, SE to set up ingestion test once S3 details provided. Starlight: provide SAML metadata and S3 test bucket, schedule procurement review meeting.
[23:05] Ben: can we get a calendar invite for the procurement vendor review?
[23:12] Maya: I'll have procurement propose times.
[23:40] Priya: I'll share S3 creds and metadata by EOD.
[24:05] Liam: Great, we'll follow up in email with attachments. Any other risks or blockers?
[24:20] Tom: no major blockers beyond procurement sign-off.
[24:35] Maya: just to flag data residency — for certain products we may need EU-only storage; we might ask for model routing by region later.
[25:00] Sofia: we support region routing and will document options — for hosted we have regions in NA and EU.
[25:40] Ben: last question — are there any issues with having truncated prompts in logs for debugging? we sometimes need more context.
[25:55] Liam: For Dedicated/Private you can opt-in to store full request payloads with retention controls; for hosted we can enable it under stricter controls and higher cost.
[26:25] Maya: okay. if procurement signs off we aim to start pilot rollout next week.
[26:40] Liam: Sounds good. We'll prioritize SOC2 and logs.
[27:05] Sofia: I'll also include an example of the SAML assertion and attribute mappings.
[27:30] Priya: thanks.
[27:40] Ben: thanks everyone.
[27:50] Liam: Quick note — we'll also include a short checklist for fintech compliance items so you can hand that to procurement.
[28:10] Maya: appreciated.
[28:30] Liam: Anything else?
[28:38] Tom: nope.
[28:42] Maya: no.
[28:50] Liam: ok thanks, we'll send the materials and reconvene next week, same time unless you want to change.
[29:10] Ben: same time works.
[29:20] Priya: thanks all.
[29:30] Liam: thanks everyone — meeting over.
